previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute worsening of lower back pain one month after lumbar spine fusion and discectomy. He presented with increased pain at the surgical site radiating down both legs, but without fever, neurological deficits, or signs of infection. Imaging showed no hardware failure or fractures. Pain was managed with scheduled ketorolac, acetaminophen, and increased gabapentin, with oxycodone for breakthrough pain. Constipation developed during admission and was treated with senna, docusate, bisacodyl, and magnesium citrate, leading to resolution. His diabetes was managed with a standardized insulin regimen during the stay, and he was advised to resume his home regimen post-discharge. He improved significantly, was ambulatory, and discharged home with follow-up planned with orthopedics and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient is a ___ with h/o CAD s/p multiple stents, PE, DM, 
HTN, HLP who presented with sudden chest pain and shortness of 
breath concerning for angina.
.  
# ACS:
Patient with significant history of CAD presenting with chest 
pain concerning for acute coronary syndrome. He had mild 
elevation of troponin. Patient underwent cardiac catheterization 
which revealed three vessel coronary artery disease and 
progression of CAD in the proximal-mid LAD and in the diffusely 
diseased mid and distal LAD. A DES was successfully placed in 
the proximal-mid LAD and balloon angioplasty of the mid and 
near-apical LAD was performed. The patient was also noted to 
have evidence of microvascular disease. The patient was chest 
pain free following procedure. He was instructed to continue ASA 
325mg x one month and should thereafter continue on ASA 81mg for 
life. Plavix 75mg should be continued for at least one year. 
Patient to follow up with his cardiologist upon discharge.

Metoprolol.

resumed upon discharge.
